"Implement the solution in src/main/java/VariableLengthQuantity.java so that the tests in src/test/java/VariableLengthQuantityTest.java pass. The specification follows.

# Instructions

Implement variable length quantity encoding and decoding.

The goal of this exercise is to implement [VLQ][vlq] encoding/decoding.

In short, the goal of this encoding is to encode integer values in a way that would save bytes.
Only the first 7 bits of each byte are significant (right-justified; sort of like an ASCII byte).
So, if you have a 32-bit value, you have to unpack it into a series of 7-bit bytes.
Of course, you will have a variable number of bytes depending upon your integer.
To indicate which is the last byte of the series, you leave bit #7 clear.
In all of the preceding bytes, you set bit #7.

So, if an integer is between `0-127`, it can be represented as one byte.
Although VLQ can deal with numbers of arbitrary sizes, for this exercise we will restrict ourselves to only numbers that fit in a 32-bit unsigned integer.
Here are examples of integers as 32-bit values, and the variable length quantities that they translate to:

```text
 NUMBER        VARIABLE QUANTITY
00000000              00
00000040              40
0000007F              7F
00000080             81 00
00002000             C0 00
00003FFF             FF 7F
00004000           81 80 00
00100000           C0 80 00
001FFFFF           FF FF 7F
00200000          81 80 80 00
08000000          C0 80 80 00
0FFFFFFF          FF FF FF 7F
```

[vlq]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variable-length_quantity


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper classes may go only in the solution's package."

Now I understand the structure. Let's analyze the requirements:

1. `encode(List<Long> numbers)` — takes a list of numbers and returns a list of hex strings like "0x0", "0x81", etc.
2. `decode(List<Long> bytes)` — takes a list of bytes (as Long) and returns a list of hex strings like "0x7f", "0x2000", etc.

Important details:
- Encoding: each number is encoded as VLQ bytes. Only the lower 7 bits of each byte are significant. Bit 7 (0x80) is set on all bytes except the last.
- The hex strings are lowercase (e.g., "0x0", "0x40", "0x7f", "0x81", "0xc0", "0xff", "0xffffffff").

Let's look at the format of the expected output:
- "0x0" — lowercase hex, no leading zeros
- "0x40", "0x7f", "0x81", "0xc0", "0xff"
- "0x2000", "0x1fffff", "0xffffffff"

So the format is "0x" + lowercase hex of the value.

For encoding:
- Input numbers are Long values (32-bit unsigned integers).
- Each number is encoded into VLQ bytes.
- Output is a flat list of hex strings.

For decoding:
- Input bytes are Long values (each representing a byte).
- Each byte has 7 significant bits. Bit 7 indicates continuation.
- Output is a list of hex strings of the decoded values.
- If the sequence is incomplete (i.e., the last byte has bit 7 set), throw IllegalArgumentException with the message "Invalid variable-length quantity encoding".

Let's think about the encoding algorithm:
```java
List<String> encode(List<Long> numbers) {
    List<String> result = new ArrayList<>();
    for (Long number : numbers) {
        // Encode each number
        long value = number;
        List<Long> bytes = new ArrayList<>();
        bytes.add(value & 0x7F); // First, the lowest-order 7 bits
        value >>= 7;
        while (value > 0) {
            bytes.add(0x80 | (value & 0x7F));
            value >>= 7;
        }
        // Reverse so that the highest-order byte comes first
        Collections.reverse(bytes);
        for (Long b : bytes) {
            result.add(formatHex(b));
        }
    }
    return result;
}
```

- Take the lowest-order 7 bits as the first byte, and set bit 7 (continuation flag).
- Continue with the next 7 bits, and so on.
- The last byte (highest-order) has bit 7 clear.

So for 0x80 (128 = 0b10000000):
- Lowest 7 bits: 0x00, with continuation → 0x80
- Next 7 bits: 0x01 → 0x01

- Group 1: 0b1 = 0x01

So the encoding writes the highest-order group first, and sets the continuation bit on all bytes except the last.

VLQ (like MIDI's VLQ, or the one in the spec):

The spec says: "To indicate which is the last byte of the series, you leave bit #7 clear. In all of the preceding bytes, you set bit #7."

So bit 7 is set on all bytes except the last. The last byte has bit 7 clear.

```
00000080             81 00
```

If we write from the highest-order group to the lowest-order group:
- 128 = 0b1_0000000
- Highest group: 1 (0x01)
- Lowest group: 0 (0x00)

- First byte (not last, so continuation): 0x01 | 0x80 = 0x81
- Last byte (no continuation): 0x00

So the encoding writes from the highest-order group to the lowest-order group. The last byte (lowest-order group) has bit 7 clear, and all preceding bytes (higher-order groups) have bit 7 set.

- Group 1 (next 7 bits): 0b0000000 = 0x00

- Group 1: 0x40, continuation → 0xC0

So the algorithm is:
1. Split the number into 7-bit groups.
2. Write from the highest-order group to the lowest-order group.
3. Set bit 7 on all bytes except the last (lowest-order group).

Approach:
```java
List<String> encode(List<Long> numbers) {
    List<String> result = new ArrayList<>();
    for (Long number : numbers) {
        long value = number;
        // Collect groups from lowest to highest
        List<Long> groups = new ArrayList<>();
        groups.add(value & 0x7F);
        value >>= 7;
        while (value > 0) {
            groups.add(value & 0x7F);
            value >>= 7;
        }
        // Write from highest to lowest, setting the continuation bit on all except the last
        for (int i = groups.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
            long byte = groups.get(i);
            if (i > 0) {
                byte |= 0x80; // Set continuation bit on all bytes except the last (i==0)
            }
            result.add("0x" + Long.toHexString(byte));
        }
    }
    return result;
}
```

We iterate from i = groups.size()-1 (highest) down to i=0 (lowest).

When i > 0 (not the lowest group, i.e., not the last byte to be written), set the continuation bit.
When i == 0 (the lowest group, the last byte to be written), don't set the continuation bit.

```java
List<String> decode(List<Long> bytes) {
    List<String> result = new ArrayList<>();
    long value = 0;
    boolean inSequence = false;
    for (int i = 0; i < bytes.size(); i++) {
        long byte = bytes.get(i);
        value = (value << 7) | (byte & 0x7F);
        inSequence = true;
        if ((byte & 0x80) == 0) {
            // Last byte of the sequence
            result.add("0x" + Long.toHexString(value));
            value = 0;
            inSequence = false;
        }
    }
    if (inSequence) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid variable-length quantity encoding");
    }
    return result;
}
```

import java.util.ArrayList;

class VariableLengthQuantity {

    private static final int CONTINUATION_BIT = 0x80;
    private static final int SIGNIFICANT_BITS = 0x7F;

    List<String> encode(List<Long> numbers) {
        List<String> result = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Long number : numbers) {
            long value = number;
            // Collect 7-bit groups from least significant to most significant.
            List<Long> groups = new ArrayList<>();
            groups.add(value & SIGNIFICANT_BITS);
            value >>= 7;
            while (value > 0) {
                groups.add(value & SIGNIFICANT_BITS);
                value >>= 7;
            }
            // Emit from most significant group to least significant.
            // All bytes except the last carry the continuation bit.
            for (int i = groups.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
                long byte = groups.get(i);
                if (i > 0) {
                    byte |= CONTINUATION_BIT;
                }

            }
        }
        return result;
    }

                value = 0;
                inSequence = false;
            }
        }
        if (inSequence) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid variable-length quantity encoding");
        }
        return result;
    }
